name: When should I hire a handyman instead of a licensed general contractor?

mainEntity.name: When should I hire a handyman instead of a licensed general contractor?

acceptedAnswer.text: A handyman is ideal for minor repairs and cosmetic updates, while a licensed general contractor is needed for structural changes, significant additions, or heavy trade coordination. For instance, fixing a cracked tile or patching drywall falls under handyman work. However, moving plumbing lines, rewiring a panel, or removing load-bearing walls requires comprehensive contracting management. At HH Remodeling, owner Abraham Becerra provides both capabilities: acting as a hands-on contractor who handles carpentry, drywall, and finish work directly, while bringing in trusted specialty trade partners when plumbing or electrical permits become necessary.
acceptedAnswer.description: Hire a handyman for minor fixes, drywall repair, and trim work. Choose a general contractor when projects require structural changes, permits, or trade coordination.
